paper.title: Thompson Sampling: An Asymptotically Optimal Finite Time Analysis

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-armed bandit with Bernoulli rewards
settings.definition_quote: Associated with each action, $a$, is an unknown Bernoulli distribution $\cB\left(\mu_a\right)$, whose expectation is $\mu_a$. At each time $t$ the agent chooses to observe an action $A_t\in\{1,\dots,K\}$ and receives a reward $R_t$ drawn from the distribution $\cB\left(\mu_{A_t}\right)$.

symbols.epsilon: arbitrary positive slack (not a PAC accuracy)

extra_assumptions: unique optimal arm (assumed in analysis; paper argues WLOG)

source.quote: For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists a problem-dependent constant $C(\epsilon,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K)$ such that the regret of Thompson Sampling satisfies: \[ \cR(T)\leq(1+\epsilon)\sum_{a\in A:\mu_a\neq\mu^*}\frac{\Delta_a(\ln(T)+\ln\ln(T))}{K(\mu_a,\mu^*)}+ C(\epsilon,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K). \]

results.notes: Regret defined via expected pull counts (pseudo-regret). Thompson Sampling does not use T; the ln ln T only arises in the analysis, so horizon marked anytime. Implies asymptotic optimality matching Lai-Robbins.

bound.regime: for every epsilon > 0, each suboptimal arm a

extra_assumptions: unique optimal arm, mu_1 > mu_2 >= ... >= mu_K

source.label: Thm2Arm
source.quote: Let $\epsilon>0$. With $b$ as in Proposition \ref{important:lemma}, for every suboptimal arm $a$, there exist constants $D(\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a)$, $N(b,\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a)$ and $N_0(b)$ such that: \bE[N_{a,T}] \leq (1+\epsilon)\frac{\ln(T) + \ln\ln (T) }{K(\mu_a,\mu_1)} + D(\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a) + N(b,\epsilon,\mu_1,\mu_a)+N_0(b) + 5 + 2C_b .

results.notes: Bound on the expected number of pulls E[N_{a,T}] of a suboptimal arm, hence quantity 'other'.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit (Bernoulli case as stated), strongly consistent policies; lower bound on expected pulls of each suboptimal arm

bound.regime: T -> infinity, normalized by ln T

cited_results.cited_title: Finite-time analysis of the multiarmed bandit problem
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit; expected pulls of a suboptimal arm
